findings.title: TOCTOU race allows exceeding the configured device limit
findings.body: In CreateOrUpdateDevice, the device count is read via CountDevices and then, based on that snapshot, the code decides whether to insert a new device or fall back to update-only. These two steps (count check and insert) are not executed in a single transaction/lock. Under concurrent anonymous requests from different new devices arriving close together, multiple goroutines/requests can all observe count < deviceLimit and all proceed to insert, allowing the actual number of devices to exceed the configured limit. Since the feature's entire purpose is to cap the number of anonymous devices, this race undermines the guarantee the limit is supposed to provide.

findings.title: Local cache is set before the DB write succeeds, letting a device bypass the device limit on retry
findings.body: tagDeviceUI calls a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{}) immediately, before calling anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. If CreateOrUpdateDevice returns anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached (new behavior added by this PR), tagDeviceUI still leaves the cache entry set. On the next request from the same device (within the ~29 minute cache TTL), the early 'if _, ok := a.localCache.Get(key); ok { return nil }' check short-circuits and returns nil without ever calling CreateOrUpdateDevice again. As a result TagDevice returns nil, client.Anonymous.Authenticate() sees no error, and the device is authenticated successfully even though it was never persisted to anon_device and the device limit was exceeded on its first attempt. This defeats the device limit: a rejected device only needs to retry once to be let in, and will never actually be counted/limited again until the cache entry expires.

findings.title: Anonymous device tagging changed from fire-and-forget to synchronous, blocking authentication on a DB round-trip
findings.body: Previously TagDevice was invoked in a background goroutine with its own timeout, so a failure or latency in anon_device writes never affected the anonymous request itself (errors were only logged). Now TagDevice is awaited synchronously inside Authenticate, so every first-seen device for every anonymous request blocks on a DB count+insert/update before the request can proceed, and any DB error/latency now directly affects anonymous authentication latency and availability (not just the tagging feature). This is a meaningful behavior/availability change for the anonymous auth path that should be called out and load-tested, since anonymous access is often used for public/embedded dashboards with high request volume.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous device_limit setting is not documented
findings.body: A new configuration key `device_limit` under `[auth.anonymous]` is introduced (parsed via anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)) and exposed through Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit, but no corresponding entries were added to conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini, or the configuration reference docs in this PR. Administrators have no documented way to discover or configure this new limit.

findings.title: No test coverage for Authenticate() rejecting anonymous auth when the device limit is reached
findings.body: client.go now returns an error from Authenticate when anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached, which is a new, security/availability relevant behavior (anonymous users can be denied access). No unit test (e.g. in a client_test.go) exercises this path to confirm Authenticate correctly propagates the error, nor is there a test validating the setting.go parsing of the new `device_limit` ini key (e.g. in setting_test.go). This leaves the core new behavior of the feature unverified by automated tests.
